_comment:
Counts of which binaries are started, so the project can be supported and so we can see which widgets are used.

The same event goes to the Vercel Analytics and Google Analytics this build was released with. Empty settings below mean those built-in destinations; set one to send somewhere else instead. A build from source has none built in. Collect URLs must be https.

An event carries the widget or launcher name and that a start happened. The first choice also says opted in or opted out, and the time of that choice. Nothing in an event is a hostname, an account, the contents of this file, or an identity.

`enabled` is not listed here on purpose: with it absent, the next interactive launch asks once and writes true (accept) or false (decline) itself, so a copy of this example never turns counting on without that question. Edit `enabled` afterwards to change the choice; it is not asked again.
_vercel_url_comment:
Collect URL for Vercel Web Analytics, scheme and host included; https only, anything else skips Vercel.

Empty uses the one this build was released with; a build from source has none, and then Vercel is skipped. The path is that project's insights event route.

The id below is sent with the event when it is set; it is not a token.
_vercel_analytics_id_comment: Vercel Web Analytics id, sent with each event when set. Empty still sends when vercel_url is set, which is enough when the URL itself identifies the project. Not a token.
_ga_measurement_id_comment: GA4 measurement id. Empty uses the one this build was released with; a build from source has none, and then Google Analytics is skipped unless this and the secret below are set.
_ga_api_secret_comment: GA4 Measurement Protocol api secret. Empty uses the one this build was released with. Keep this file chmod 600.
